blueprint_topic: Management of Care — integrating palliative/supportive care into chronic heart-failure management
stem: A client with chronic heart failure is continuing disease-directed therapy. The family asks why the team is also discussing palliative and supportive care. Which response by the RN is most accurate?

options.A: Palliative care can be incorporated throughout heart-failure care to address symptoms, communication, goals, uncertainty, and caregiver needs.
options.B: Palliative care is generally introduced after heart-failure therapies stop so the plan can shift from disease management to symptom-focused care.
options.C: Palliative care is mainly useful when symptoms become refractory because earlier communication and caregiver support remain part of routine cardiology care.
options.D: Palliative consultation usually replaces longitudinal heart-failure follow-up once goals-of-care discussions become a major part of the treatment plan.

rationale: A is correct. Section 13.1 of the 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA heart-failure guideline states that palliative care should be integrated into the care of patients with heart failure and that palliative/supportive approaches should be incorporated throughout the course of illness. The guideline describes high-quality communication, prognosis and uncertainty discussions, shared decision-making, advance care planning, relief of physical and emotional distress, and attention to family-caregiver needs as components of this care. B is incorrect because palliative care is not contingent on stopping disease-directed heart-failure therapy. C is incorrect because the guideline places communication, uncertainty, goals, and caregiver support within palliative care across the illness course rather than restricting its relevance to refractory symptoms. D is incorrect because palliative/supportive care is integrated into overall heart-failure care rather than functioning as a replacement for longitudinal heart-failure management.
educational_objective: Explain that palliative and supportive care is integrated throughout the heart-failure illness course to address symptoms, communication, goals and uncertainty, decision-making, and caregiver needs rather than being reserved for a later treatment phase.
source_organization: American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/Heart Failure Society of America
source_document_title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
source_version_date: Originally published April 1, 2022 with subsequent corrections; current ACC Heart Failure Guideline Hub still lists the 2022 guideline, and ACC Clinical Policy in Progress updated June 15, 2026 schedules the Heart Failure guideline update for 2027; sources rechecked 2026-08-20
source_locator: Section 13.1 — Palliative and Supportive Care, Shared Decision-Making, and End-of-Life, Synopsis: palliative care should be integrated into the care of patients with HF; components include high-quality communication, prognosis/anticipatory guidance/uncertainty, shared decision-making, advance care planning, attention to physical/emotional/spiritual/psychological distress, relief of suffering, inclusion of family caregivers, and care coordination. Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text 1: palliative and supportive approaches are inherent to overall HF care and should be incorporated throughout the course of illness by health care professionals. ACC Heart Failure Guideline Hub currently lists the 2022 guideline; ACC Clinical Policy in Progress updated June 15, 2026 lists a Heart Failure guideline update for 2027.
source_claim_supported: Current HF guidance supports integrating palliative/supportive care throughout the heart-failure illness course and includes symptom relief, communication about prognosis and uncertainty, shared decision-making/advance care planning, and family-caregiver support; it is not contingent on stopping disease-directed HF care.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care — Referrals/Continuity of Care: assess referral needs, collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, coordinate/manage care, and follow up unresolved care issues. Physiological Integrity — Basic Care and Comfort — Nonpharmacological Comfort Interventions: assess need for palliative care/symptom management and counsel clients regarding palliative care/symptom management.
pdf_visual_verification: Relevant NCSBN Management of Care referral/continuity content was visually verified earlier in this 2026-08-20 audit session. The NCSBN palliative-care activity statements were verified textually from the official PDF; the prior screenshot request for that palliative-care page returned CACHE MISS, so no visual verification of that page is claimed.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'heart failure palliative supportive care hospice goals caregiver throughout illness' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Retained the heart-failure palliative-care construct but removed all/only-style cueing and the uniquely long key. The revised distractors test realistic timing, symptom-threshold, and care-model misconceptions while avoiding a universal hospice or treatment-withdrawal caricature.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly reflects Section 13.1 integration across the illness course and its symptom, communication, goals/uncertainty, and caregiver components.
option_audit.B: Plausible late-phase misconception; incorrect because palliative/supportive care is not conditional on stopping disease-directed HF therapy.
option_audit.C: Plausible symptom-threshold misconception; incorrect because the guideline includes communication, uncertainty, decision-making, and caregiver support throughout HF care.
option_audit.D: Plausible specialty-replacement misconception; incorrect because palliative/supportive care is integrated into overall HF care rather than replacing longitudinal HF management.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All four responses contain comparable explanatory detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel explanations responding to the family's question.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after AHA/ACC/HFSA source-based reread.
